hero.headline: Photography shaped by movement, landscape, and time outside.
hero.intro: Landscape and portrait photographer specializing in climbing, with a growing practice in web-based creative work.

about.heading: Photography, climbing, and the places where they meet.
paragraphs: I started taking photographs in 2012 with a family iPhone. Most of the early images were of nature and close-up shots of flowers around our property. I was drawn to how beautiful it all was and wanted to see whether I could capture some of that beauty with a camera.

During my senior year of high school, I made a self-portrait and fell in love with editing it. Later, I took a photography class in college for fun. The professor pulled me aside and suggested that I consider switching majors. I eventually did, earning my BS in Commercial Photography from Appalachian State University in 2020, after switching from studying computer science.

project.heading: Learning to pay attention.
paragraphs:
Before photography became a serious part of my life, soccer had been my lifelong passion. I knew it was not something I could continue forever, particularly as injuries became more of a concern, so I started climbing as another way to stay active.

It clicked almost immediately. I still cannot entirely explain why it connected with my brain so strongly, but more than a decade later, the passion has never gone away.

Climbing connects me with nature in a physical and immediate way. Moving across rock requires close attention to texture, shape, and the smallest details of a surface. That way of looking carries into my photography. Photographing climbers also creates its own opportunities: the movement is often epic, and the places where climbing happens are usually beautiful.

I built the custom editor behind the site as a way to organize and shape that archive on my own terms. Like the work it contains, the system will continue to change as new projects, ideas, and forms are added.

additional.heading: A portfolio, an experiment, and an ongoing personal project.
paragraphs:
I built this website because I did not want to pay for a portfolio platform when I knew I was capable of making one myself. I had also wanted to create a virtual 3D gallery for years. What began as a practical decision became another creative project.

Photography and coding both act as lightning rods for my focus. Each gives me somewhere to direct my attention, make something tangible, and experience the satisfaction of finishing something that did not exist before.

This site brings those interests together. First and foremost, it is a personal project that I started for fun. It is also a professional portfolio, an archive of my work, and a place where I can continue experimenting. Over time, I want it to grow beyond photography to include web-based art, videos, and other digital projects.

contact.headline: Work With Me
contact.body: Available for selected photographic assignments, collaborations, and web projects. If you are interested in working together on an image-based project or a custom portfolio site, get in touch.
